title: Orgrimmar
body: Orgrimmar is the capital of the Horde, carved into a canyon of red stone in the mountains of northern Durotar. Thrall raised it after the battle at Mount Hyjal, when he led his people to this harsh coast, and named it for Orgrim Doomhammer, the friend and mentor who had passed the Horde into his hands. Goblins, tauren and the Darkspear trolls helped to build it. The city is a maze of valleys joined by tunnels and ramps: the Valley of Strength behind the great gate, the Drag and the Cleft of Shadow, the Valley of Honor where warriors and hunters train, the troll quarter of the Valley of Spirits, and the Valley of Wisdom, where the Warchief holds court in Grommash Hold. Orcs and trolls share its streets with tauren, Forsaken and, of late, blood elves. Not every enemy lies outside the walls. Demon cultists gather in Ragefire Chasm, the caverns beneath the city. And when traitors seized the Undercity after the Wrathgate, Orgrimmar shut its shops, took in the Forsaken who fled, and lived under martial law.

title: Valley of Strength
body: Past the great gate of Orgrimmar lies the Valley of Strength. Here stand the bank, the auction house and the tower where wind riders come and go, and here too is the Broken Tusk, where Innkeeper Gryshka bids weary fighters lay their axes by the fire and tell of their battles, while a drunkard named Gamon holds up the bar. Overlord Runthak keeps order in the valley, and it is here that the head of the slain Nefarian is mounted for all to see. In the dark days after the Wrathgate the valley changed. Shops were shuttered by order of the Warchief, merchants grumbled about lost gold, and Forsaken refugees crowded the approach, begging for help.

title: Valley of Wisdom
body: North of the Valley of Strength rises the Valley of Wisdom, the high seat of the city. Grommash Hold stands here, the Warchief's own fortress, and nearby the armor of Mannoroth the Destructor is displayed upon a great trunk. A plaque signed by Thrall names Mannoroth as the demon who first cursed the orcs with bloodlust, and bids the Horde remember how far it has come and how hard it fought to regain its honor. The wisdom of the spirits dwells here too. Shaman trainers of orc, troll and tauren blood teach in the valley, and the elder far seer Zor Lonetree, well schooled in the politics of the Alliance, sends young heroes wherever the land cries out for aid.

title: Grommash Hold
body: Grommash Hold is the fortress of the Warchief, built into the cliffs of the Valley of Wisdom and bearing the name of Grom Hellscream, whose blow slew Mannoroth and freed the orcs from the demon's curse. Guards still call it Thrall's Fortress. Its throne room is thick walled and windowless, and the Kor'kron, the Warchief's elite bodyguard, stand watch at every turn. Old Eitrigg and Vol'jin of the Darkspear counsel Thrall at his side, an ambassador of Silvermoon speaks softly for the blood elves, and a guest named Mokvar, granted sanctuary by Thrall, takes care to bring his host no trouble. When traitors seized the Undercity, it was through portals opened here that the Horde went to take it back.

title: Cleft of Shadow
body: Off the Drag, a crevasse splits the rock of Orgrimmar, open only to a strip of sky, and in its gloom live the city's less savory folk. Warlocks of the Horde train here, insisting that the arcane corrupts only the weak, and the warlock Neeru Fireblade keeps a hut, proclaiming his loyalty to the Warchief. Rogues of the Shattered Hand teach stealth, deception and poison. At the bottom of the cleft opens Ragefire Chasm, the burning caverns beneath the city, where the cult of the Searing Blade hides under the felguard Taragaman the Hungerer and works in secret to lead innocent members of the Horde astray.

title: Valley of Honor
body: The Valley of Honor, in the northeast of the city, is Orgrimmar's martial quarter. Warriors drill in the Hall of the Brave, where officers of the Horde army muster and battlemasters send fighters to Alterac, Warsong Gulch and other fields of war. Hunters learn to hunt with pride, honor and tradition in their own hall, smiths and miners work the forges, and Ogunaro Wolfrunner keeps kennels of finely bred wolves, offered only to those the orcs count as true friends. Arena organizers gather challengers for the Ring of Valor. Not everything here is war. An orphanage shelters children who lost their parents to the Horde's many conflicts, a quiet reminder of the price of all that glory.

title: Valley of Spirits
body: The Valley of Spirits, a long and narrow valley in the southwest of the city, reached from the Valley of Strength, has long been the quarter of the Darkspear trolls. Their huts and lodges crowd its slopes. In Darkbriar Lodge troll mages teach the arcane arts, and a portal on its upper floor opens onto the Blasted Lands, far across the sea. The troll priests nearby greet strangers with a warning to respect their ways, or have a curse laid on them and theirs. Snakes of every color are for sale at Xan'tish's stall and staves at Ukra'nor's, and Warcaller Gorlach has the latest news from both continents and beyond for any hero willing to listen.

title: Thrall
body: Thrall, son of Durotan, is Warchief of the Horde. Born a Frostwolf and raised a gladiator slave in Durnholde Keep, he broke free, learned the ways of the shaman and freed the orcs from the internment camps, taking up the Doomhammer from the dying Orgrim. He led them across the sea to found Durotar. From Grommash Hold he preaches a new Horde: no demon spawned army, but a people of wisdom and honor who know when to show compassion even to a foe. He guards a fragile peace with the Alliance, was shaken to learn that a grandmother he never knew lives in Outland, and when Varimathras and Putress seized the Undercity, he swore that justice would be served.

title: Vol'jin
body: Vol'jin, son of Sen'jin, leads the Darkspear trolls. When Thrall's orcs freed his people from their captors on a storm swept isle, where his father was slain, Vol'jin pledged the tribe to the Horde, and the trolls followed the orcs to Kalimdor. Now he stands in the Warchief's chamber as an adviser, greeting each new champion as a sign that the fates smile on the Horde. He has no love for humans. When Admiral Proudmoore's sealed orders came to Orgrimmar, he reminded all who would hear that he had urged Thrall countless times not to trust them. When the Undercity fell to traitors, it was Vol'jin who held the ground outside the ruins until Thrall and Sylvanas arrived.

title: Eitrigg
body: Eitrigg is an old warrior of the Blackrock clan, a veteran of the First and Second Wars. After the second he followed Rend Blackhand to Blackrock Spire, where both his sons were slain in the wars with the Dark Iron dwarves. Refusing to serve such a power hungry fool, he went to live as a hermit in the woods of Lordaeron near Hearthglen. Captured there by humans, he was saved from execution by Tirion Fordring and by Thrall, whose vision of a Horde free of demons won him back. He became an adviser in the Warchief's throne room. Now Tirion, Highlord of the Argent Crusade, has asked for him, and Eitrigg serves the Crusade at the Argent Stand in Zul'Drak.

title: Neeru Fireblade
body: Neeru Fireblade is the orc warlock of the Cleft of Shadow who claims he volunteered to aid the young Warchief, to prove that not every warlock of the Horde would rule it or destroy it from within. He counsels strangers not to trust too quickly, or distrust, for even friends serve their own ends. Shamans send him cult relics they cannot read, and heroes bring him trophies of the Searing Blade and even Onyxia's head. To a supposed fellow cultist, though, he speaks freely: Thrall is a fool, and the Burning Legion will drain this world and make ash of it. Thrall knows him for the true leader of the Burning Blade, and uses him.

title: Overlord Runthak
body: Overlord Runthak stands in the Valley of Strength, the orc who carries out the Warchief's commands without question. It falls to him to proclaim the Horde's great victories to the people of Orgrimmar. When Nefarian fell, he took up the proclamation once made by High Overlord Saurfang before Saurfang went north, crying the dragon's death to the gathered city and mounting the head of the beast for all to see. His hardest hour came after the Wrathgate. With the Undercity lost and war with the Alliance at hand, he faced an angry crowd and shouted it into silence: the shops would stay closed until further notice, and the Warchief was doing all he could to keep them safe.

title: Shenthul
body: Shenthul is a jungle troll of high rank in the Shattered Hand, the order of spies, assassins and poisoners whose rogues train in the Cleft of Shadow. The Hand names itself the veil over Kalimdor: its protectors, police, judges, jury and executioners. It counts the Deathstalkers of the Undercity as allies, and its spies have crept into the upper halls of Blackrock Spire. Even Thrall, its fence Jes'rimon claims, admits the Hand is needed. Its loyalty is less certain. Shenthul warns his recruits to stay vigilant against the changes Thrall would bring, since numbers alone will not overcome his rule, and his trainers speak openly of restoring the Horde's glory without the Warchief's timidity.

title: Hidden Enemies
body: Thrall will not tolerate traitors, but neither will he strike too soon and leave the rot to spread. So he turns to a young hero who can go where his agents cannot. The first task is to take an insignia from a Burning Blade lieutenant at Skull Rock. With it the hero calls on Neeru Fireblade in the Cleft of Shadow, whom Thrall knows to be the true leader of the Burning Blade, and Neeru, taking the newcomer for one of his own, speaks of the cult and of the leaders of the Searing Blade he values most. Thrall marks those leaders first. In Ragefire Chasm the satyr Bazzalan and Jergosh the Invoker are slain, and Neeru rages at the loss, blaming Thrall's do-gooders. Still trusting his new lieutenant, he lets slip that his agents in the Barrens and Ashenvale will begin the Shadow Council's newest scheme. Thrall had heard nothing of the Council in Ashenvale. His spies will look into it, and the Warchief will call on his hero again.

title: The False Warchief
body: Among documents taken from Blackrock Spire by the Kargath Expeditionary Force lies a claim that stuns Orgrimmar: Rend Blackhand, long thought dead, lives and calls himself Warchief. The news goes first to Eitrigg in Thrall's chamber, for none knows the Blackrock better. He tells how Rend and his brother Maim fled to the Spire after the Second War and fought the Dark Iron dwarves for it, driving them into the lower city only after Maim died and the dragons came, how his own sons fell in that war, and how Nefarian, brood of Deathwing, now rules the Spire with Rend as his servant. Thrall's answer is plain. Whoever goes must find a way through the Halls of Ascension, slay the false Warchief and lay his head before the throne. When it is done, Thrall calls on all Orgrimmar to honor its heroes and bathes the city in his blessing, and the Blackrock are thrown into chaos once more.

title: What the Wind Carries
body: After Rend's fall, Thrall shares what the wind carries from the Eastern Kingdoms. The Shattered Hand's spies in Blackrock Spire have learned that Onyxia, brood mother of the black dragonflight, had disguised herself as a noble of Stormwind's court and bent its regent to her will, until she was unmasked and fled to her lair in Dustwallow Marsh. Asked why not let the Alliance fall, Thrall only laughs. The Horde has peace, something its people have not known for ages, and he will not throw that away. But Onyxia cannot live so near the Horde's cities. His champion Rexxar found a way into her lair before leaving for Outland, and left the secret with his companion Rokaro in Shadowprey Village. Rokaro sets the hero on the road: an illusion woven by Myranda the Hag, the trials of the old drake Emberstrife, and at last an amulet that only the blood of General Drakkisath can awaken. With it the way into the lair of the brood mother lies open, and the victory, Rokaro promises, will be remembered for many years.

title: The Lord of Blackrock
body: Nefarian, son of Deathwing, ruled Blackrock Spire from its heights and kept the false Warchief Rend in his service. When at last the dragon's battle scarred head is carried down from his lair and brought to Orgrimmar, Thrall wishes only that he could have seen the beast's face at the killing blow. Yet he gives a warning with his thanks: the son of Deathwing lies dead, and surely the evil one stirs. He sends the slayer to Overlord Runthak in the Valley of Strength. There, before the gathered city, Runthak cries out that Nefarian is slain, that the blow will surely rouse the Aspects from their malaise, and that Deathwing himself reels in pain and anguish this day. Then the head of the beast is mounted for all to see.

title: Alliance Relations
body: Craven Drok shares a truth about the orcs that is far from obvious. They are a proud people, and the war with the humans tried even Thrall's patience, but the Warchief is a diplomat at heart, and in his years among humans he learned much of their ways. Craven sends the curious to Keldran, a student of magic and other mystical arts whose hovel stands near the city's western exit. It begins with appearances, Keldran explains: how the Horde sees itself, how its allies see it and, most of all, how its enemies see it. As the Alliance pushes deeper into Kalimdor, it might wrongly decide that the Horde has made pacts with the Burning Legion, and Thrall cannot allow that. With his blessing Keldran has sent agents to Desolace to root out the Burning Blade and the satyr there. When the work is done, Keldran gives thanks: Thrall desires peace, and a Horde seen to be clean of demons gives the Alliance no cause for needless war.

title: The Shattered Hand
body: Young rogues of the Horde who show promise are approached quietly. In Razor Hill, Kaplak passes word that Therzok of the Cleft of Shadow has an offer to make. The offer is a test. The Warchief, Therzok says, is too subtle and too cautious to unleash the might of the Horde, and the Shattered Hand means to win back the pride of the old conquerors, building strength in the shadows and striking where the enemy is exposed. First the recruit must kill Tazan, a troll who trades with the pirates near Ratchet, and bring back his satchel. The satchel is locked and the key is not on the body, so the recruit must find Tazan's assistant Gamon, a drunkard at the tavern in Orgrimmar, and quietly relieve him of it. What lies inside proves the recruit's worth, and Therzok welcomes the newest member of the Shattered Hand.
